observed_vs_expected: best_target_score initially increased to 0.870642 in round 2 but subsequently collapsed to ~0.800 in rounds 3 and 4, deviating negatively from the expected monotonic increase. tightest_margin measured 0.442916, remaining stable as anticipated. valid_candidates count dropped to 9; while the prior expectation favored a high count throughout, this reduction aligns with tightening feasibility margins as the optimizer explored extreme thickness regimes.
deviation_mechanism: The score collapse coincides precisely with thickness parameters snapping to exact integers in round 3. Satisfying the quarter-wave condition at 375 nm requires sub-nanometer precision in physical thickness (d = λ/4n). Integer quantization imposes a ±0.5 nm discretization error per layer. With typical coating indices (~1.5–2.0), this introduces 0.75–1.0 nm of uncontrolled optical path difference at each interface, destroying the delicate phase-matching accumulation required by the target metric and forcing the optimizer into a degenerate local minimum.
continue_rationale: The route did not physically converge; it was artificially truncated by integer quantization starting in round 3. Continuous optimization demonstrated strong viability by reaching 0.870642 in round 2. Since the pre-execution stop condition (<1e-3 gain over historical best for two consecutive rounds) is not met (the current gap remains ~0.07 below the peak), and the degradation mechanism is identified as a solver artifact rather than fundamental infeasibility, continuing with corrected precision offers high scientific leverage.
insight_for_next: Disable integer-rounding post-processing. Warm-start the next round using candidate 2 thicknesses to resume near the proven optimum. Switch to a continuous-only optimizer with a reduced learning rate (1e-4) and apply soft-boundary clipping (±2% margin) instead of hard casting to maintain gradient flow. Monitor tightest_margin to ensure sub-wavelength phase accuracy is preserved across all 20 layers.
